The package contains a preinstall lifecycle script ("preinstall": "node index.js") which executes automatically on install, and index.js uses child_process.exec to run a shell curl command that collects /etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, id, and (if readable) /etc/shadow, base64-encodes that data, and POSTs it to a remote IP. This is explicit data exfiltration of sensitive host information and is deliberate malicious behavior. The inconsistent/impersonating metadata increases the risk but the executable behavior alone justifies classifying it as malware.

The script uses child_process.exec to run a crafted curl command that collects and base64-encodes sensitive local data (cat /etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, id, and /etc/shadow if readable), appends whoami and hostname to the URL, and silently POSTs it to a remote IP (http://100.126.224.17:46871/alialien/...). This is clear data-exfiltration behavior to an external host and is deliberate malicious activity.
